narrative.overview:
Kin Kitchen is a merienda tray set out on the counter: buko-white paper, white label surfaces, latik-brown ink, a pale pandan-leaf shell around the edge, ube for every action, and yema gold kept for one job, running low. It is always light. The owner asked for a bright kitchen app in baking colours that does not look like a generated template, so the kakanin colours (pandan, ube, calamansi, blueberry, strawberry) are carried by data (chart series, category dots, the icing palette) and never by chrome. The chrome is quiet: pale pandan rail and tab bar with a hairline edge, white labels pulled off it for the selected place.

The structure underneath carried over unchanged from the previous world. Home is **Today** (stat strip, orders due, tasks, running-low canisters, the next tax return). Money lists are ledger sheets; statements are white labels with locked computed lines; a recipe's price label prints cost per unit as its one large figure; an ingredient opens as a labelled canister whose fill is its stock. The Ingredients route, at the owner's request, copies Google Sheets outright (column letters, row numbers, a formula bar, blue selection, category sheet tabs), and that copy keeps its own scoped greys and blue.

Two full-bleed kitchen surfaces sit inside the same world. **Bake mode** is the recipe card propped against the flour tin: the pandan shell becomes the whole frame, the current step sits on a white label in big Bricolage, every ingredient stays in view, and timers are pills that ring and flash ube. The **cake design board** is the cake-box-lid sketch: a 4:3 board of cake outlines, named icing swatches and 56px tools on the pandan shell. Density elsewhere is operational: one-tap checks on a phone in the kitchen, whole-sheet review on a PC.
keyCharacteristics: Always light: buko-white ground, white label surfaces, latik-brown ink; no dark mode, no dark chrome.
A pale pandan shell (rail, tab bar, toasts, Bake and board frames) with a hairline `shell-3` edge and dark pandan ink.
Ube is the only action colour (primary buttons, focus, selection, the selected nav icon in duotone).
Kakanin colours live in data only: five validated chart series, the fixed category legend, the icing palette.
Yema gold means running low, and nothing else.
Anything the app works out is locked behind a lock icon on a recessed tint, never editable.
Rises and drops always carry an arrow and a figure; business figures colour by good or bad for the owner.
Phosphor icons through one vocabulary module: regular, bold where emphasised, duotone for the selected nav item.
Solid hairlines and flat surfaces; shadow only on floating layers.

rules.name: The One Job Yellow Rule
rules.body: Yema gold means running low and nothing else. No highlights, warnings, category dots, chart series or icing chrome in the yellow band.

rules.name: The Data Wears The Kakanin Rule
rules.body: Pandan, ube, calamansi, blueberry and strawberry appear as data (series, categories, icing), never as decoration. Chrome stays buko, white, latik, pale pandan and the single ube action.

rules.name: The Never Colour Alone Rule
rules.body: A rise always carries an up arrow and a signed or percentage figure; a drop a down arrow; low always says "Low" in words.

rules.name: The Fixed Legend Rule
rules.body: A category's colour comes from its position in the category list and never changes between screens, filters or sorts.

rules.name: The Good Or Bad Rule
rules.body: Ingredient prices keep their meaning: rise is a cost going up, drop a cost going down. Business figures colour by whether the move is good (pandan drop) or bad (strawberry rise) for the owner, with the arrow carrying the direction. A flat move is `ink-2` with a dash.

rules.name: The Receivables Are Not Rises Rule
rules.body: An open balance is a neutral `surface-2` pill with the amount; it takes `rise-wash` only when the order is due today or overdue and still owes. Paid is a green check and the word.

rules.name: The Order Status Rule
rules.body: Order status uses neutral, ube wash and shell only: To do on white, Baking on `accent-wash`, Done on `shell`, Cancelled on `surface-2` struck through, each with icon and word. Never yema, `rise` or `drop`.

rules.name: The One Big Figure Rule
rules.body: Each label surface has exactly one large figure. The sheets are the exception: every cell sits at one size, and computed columns are marked by tint, weight and a lock, not scale.

rules.name: The One Lead Figure Rule
rules.body: A stat strip has one lead figure in a 1.7fr first column at Figure Large (Figure on phones); the rest step down to Figure Step (Title on phones). Word values are set in Bricolage at the step size.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every price, quantity, percentage, count and clock uses tabular numerals.

rules.name: The 16px Input Exception
rules.body: Inputs, selects, textareas and cell editors render at 16px or larger so iOS does not zoom on focus. Don't "fix" this back to 15px.

rules.name: The Flat Label Rule
rules.body: Label surfaces have no resting shadow. Shadow means a layer floats.

dos: **Do** keep the app always light: buko `ground`, white `surface` labels, latik `ink`.
**Do** frame the app in the pale pandan shell (rail, tab bar, toasts, Bake and board frames) separated by a `shell-3` hairline, never by a dark band.
**Do** use ube `accent` for every action and `focus` for every focus ring.
**Do** import icons only from the Phosphor vocabulary module: regular by default, bold for emphasis, duotone for the selected nav item.
**Do** keep kakanin colours in data: the five series in fixed order, the category legend, the icing palette.
**Do** keep computed values locked behind a lock on a recessed tint, never editable, with a link to their source.
**Do** make the one large figure on a label surface its computed truth, in tabular Geist 600.
**Do** pair every rise or drop with an arrow and a figure, and every low state with the word "Low".
**Do** give each stat strip one lead figure in the 1.7fr first column and step the rest down.
**Do** build money lists on the ledger sheet grammar.
**Do** keep the Ingredients Sheets copy on its scoped `.gsheet` colours.
**Do** use 10px corners for labels and controls, smaller nested radii inside them, and pills for things counted, flagged or timed.
**Do** keep inputs at 16px or larger, touch targets at 44px below 1024px, and Bake and board controls at 48 to 56px.
**Do** use the `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` ease-out for entrances and gauge fills, and drop motion and flashing under reduced motion.
donts: **Don't** add a dark mode or dark chrome.
**Don't** use yema gold for anything except running low.
**Don't** colour chrome with series, category or icing colours.
**Don't** use the Google Sheets greys or blue outside the Ingredients sheet.
**Don't** convey rise, drop or low by colour alone.
**Don't** give label surfaces a resting shadow.
**Don't** add chart series beyond the five validated ones, or reorder them.
**Don't** reassign a category's colour based on filtering or sort order.
**Don't** colour order status with yema, `rise` or `drop`.
**Don't** treat a receivable as a price rise: open balances stay neutral until due today or late.
**Don't** set words at figure size in a stat strip, or give a strip two lead figures.
**Don't** import icons from a package directly or mix icon sets.
